one_line: Rashtrakuta emperor-turned-patron and his court poet shaping early Kannada literary culture at Manyakheta.

appearance.age_look: Amoghavarsha appears as a lean, dignified man in his mid-30s; Śrī Vijaya appears as a composed, scholarly man in his early 40s.
appearance.face: Amoghavarsha has an oval face, medium-brown Deccan complexion, straight nose, neatly trimmed short beard and mustache, calm determined eyes, and a serene, slightly smiling expression; Śrī Vijaya has a slightly longer face, similar complexion, high forehead, thinner mustache and stubble, sharp observant eyes, and a thoughtful, focused expression.
appearance.hair: Amoghavarsha’s thick black hair is shoulder-length, oiled and slightly wavy, tied back in a low knot with a narrow gold band circling his head; Śrī Vijaya’s black hair is a bit shorter, combed back and gathered into a small knot at the back of the head with a simple dark cloth tie and no crown.
appearance.costume: Amoghavarsha wears a finely draped off-white cotton angavastra over both shoulders atop a fitted, long-sleeved golden-yellow tunic reaching mid-thigh, paired with cream-colored dhoti pants tied at the waist and pleated to mid-calf, bare feet in simple leather sandals, and ornamented with a modest gold neck torque, two thin gold chains, medium gold earrings, a pair of gold armlets on the upper arms, and several slim bangles on his right wrist; Śrī Vijaya wears a simpler pale cream tunic with three-quarter sleeves and a darker reddish-brown dhoti tied at the waist, his angavastra is plain unbleached cotton draped over the left shoulder and across the torso, his sandals are simple, and his jewelry is minimal—small plain metal earrings and a single dark bead necklace—evoking a scholar at court; both fabrics are plain Deccan cotton with subtle woven borders, Amoghavarsha’s borders in muted red and Śrī Vijaya’s in dark brown.
appearance.signature: Amoghavarsha holds a long palm-leaf manuscript bundle of Kavirajamarga tied with a red cord in his left hand, while Śrī Vijaya stands close at his right side holding a slender stylus and one loose palm leaf, both props clearly visible as their shared literary insignia.

ref_desc: Amoghavarsha I with Śrī Vijaya: oval-faced Deccan emperor and his scholar-poet, both medium-brown, with tied-back black hair, angavastra over tunic-and-dhoti outfits in off-white, gold and reddish-brown, modest Rashtrakuta-era jewelry, and palm-leaf Kavirajamarga manuscript plus stylus as shared signature props.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Amoghavarsha I standing beside his court poet Śrī Vijaya, both in 9th-century Rashtrakuta Deccan attire. Amoghavarsha is a lean, dignified man in his mid-30s with an oval face, medium-brown complexion, calm determined eyes, straight nose, and a neatly trimmed short beard and mustache. His thick black hair is shoulder-length, slightly wavy, and tied back in a low knot, with a narrow gold band circling his head. He wears an off-white cotton angavastra draped over both shoulders atop a fitted long-sleeved golden-yellow tunic to mid-thigh, cream dhoti pants pleated to mid-calf, and simple leather sandals. His jewelry is royal but modest: a gold neck torque, two thin gold chains, medium gold earrings, gold armlets on both upper arms, and slim bangles on his right wrist. Śrī Vijaya stands close at his right side, a composed man in his early 40s with a slightly longer face, high forehead, thinner mustache and light stubble, and sharp observant eyes with a thoughtful expression. His black hair is a bit shorter, combed back and gathered into a small knot at the back with a dark cloth tie and no crown. He wears a pale cream tunic with three-quarter sleeves, a darker reddish-brown dhoti, and a plain unbleached cotton angavastra draped over his left shoulder and across his torso, with simple sandals and minimal jewelry—small plain metal earrings and a single dark bead necklace. Use plain cotton textures with subtle woven borders, Amoghavarsha’s in muted red and Śrī Vijaya’s in dark brown. Their shared signature props are clearly shown: Amoghavarsha holds a long palm-leaf manuscript bundle of Kavirajamarga tied with a red cord in his left hand, while Śrī Vijaya holds a slender stylus and one loose palm leaf, emphasizing their collaborative literary role. Keep colors limited to golden yellow, off-white, cream, reddish brown, and dark brown, and present them front-facing with neutral heroic poses so this design can be redrawn consistently.
